task.title: Bound full history validation time and peak memory growth
task.description:
The 2026-07-30 scaling, storage, and peak-resource evidence identifies full history validation as the only Workbook path that does not scale. It is the sole superlinear scenario on both measured axes, and its peak resident memory grows with history while every other measured path stays flat.

Measured at commit 725a2838 (docs/performance/2026-07-30-performance-scaling-evidence-provenance.md):

- Task-count axis, depth 20: 370.73 ms at 100 active tasks, 2185.81 ms at 500, 6424.37 ms at 1000 (17.32x for 10x tasks). The log-log slope degrades with scale, 1.102 from 100 to 500 and 1.555 from 500 to 1000, so the cost worsens as repositories grow.
- History-depth axis, 500 active tasks: 2185.81 ms at depth 20 and 13299.73 ms at depth 100 (6.08x for 5x depth). Every other scenario is flat at 1.02x to 1.06x on this axis.
- Peak resident memory: 469,729,280 bytes SHA-1 and 520,880,128 bytes SHA-256 at 500-by-100, against a flat 29 MB for projection rebuild at both depths.
- Git-process ratio is exactly 1.00x on every axis pair (constant 7 processes), so the growth is in-process work, not Git subprocess fan-out.
- Normalizing by total operations, 1000-by-20 costs 0.321 ms per operation while 500-by-100 costs 0.266 ms per operation. Task count is the more punishing axis, so per-ref overhead dominates per-operation replay.

Scope this narrowly: reduce per-task-ref validation overhead and bound peak resident memory so full validation does not hold entire history resident. Do not change validation semantics, cache correctness, or the cached-unchanged path, which already scales well (1.03x across the depth axis).

## Root causes identified 2026-08-06 (code review at commit c453596)

Memory: the corpus is materialized three to four times over, simultaneously. runValidate (internal/cli/run.go:774) calls Validator.Validate (internal/historyvalidation/validator.go:62), which in --full mode marks every task pending with StopAt empty (validator.go:86-110) and hands all of them to one ReadTaskHistories call (validator.go:110). That builds, all live at once: the parent graph of every commit in the store as one map (internal/gitstore/operations.go:245-276), a flattened candidates slice holding every commit of every task (internal/gitstore/history.go:109-119), one cat-file --batch covering 4 objects per commit whose entire stdout is buffered into a bytes.Buffer (internal/gitstore/repository.go:242-252) and stays referenced through the parse loop (internal/gitstore/batch.go:115-119), a second per-object copy at make([]byte, int(size)) (batch.go:244), N x D decoded Snapshots retained in results (batch.go:82), and a third copy into HistoryCommit values (history.go:146-152). Nothing is released as tasks complete: histories stays referenced for the whole evaluate loop and per-task entries are never dropped (validator.go:120-140). evaluate itself is already an incremental fold needing only the parent state and the current record (validator.go:170-214) — it is simply fed fully materialized slices. Projection rebuild stays flat at 29 MB because it reads only operation.json blobs and no per-commit state checkpoints (operations.go:49).

Task-count superlinearity: two O(N^2 * D) terms, both in-process, which matches the constant Git process count.

1. Dominant: an unindexed per-task DELETE. validated_commits has PRIMARY KEY (validator_version, commit_id) and no index on task_id (internal/historyvalidation/cache.go:91-97, verified: the file contains no CREATE INDEX). Cache.Record issues, for every task in a full run, DELETE FROM validated_commits WHERE validator_version = ? AND task_id = ? (cache.go:320-327). The only usable index prefix matches every row, so each per-task DELETE scans the whole table while the table grows to N x D rows during the run: task k scans about (k-1) * D rows, summing to roughly N^2 * D / 2 row visits. Linear Git read work dominates at small N and this term overtakes as N grows, which is exactly the observed slope degradation on the task axis. The depth axis stays near-linear because D multiplies but never squares.
2. Secondary: walkCommitChain allocates a visited set pre-sized to the whole shared graph once per task, seenCommits := make(map[string]struct{}, len(graph)) at internal/gitstore/operations.go:295, where graph holds all N x D commits. 1000 tasks against a 20k-entry graph zeroes 20M slots; 500 against 50k zeroes 25M.

Linear but heavy terms that set the constant rather than the slope: one SQLite transaction per task in Record (cache.go:283, 383) under the default rollback journal with synchronous FULL and no journal pragmas anywhere, about two fsyncs per task; one unprepared single-row INSERT per validated commit (cache.go:328-339); Cache.Prepare runs two point queries per head plus a full-table task_id scan and is called twice per Validate (cache.go:176-269, validator.go:74, 148).

## Fix plan

1. Stream the object batch instead of buffering it. Start git cat-file --batch once over StdinPipe/StdoutPipe with cmd.Start, write the request block per commit, and expose per-task iteration from gitstore, for example ReadTaskHistoriesStream(ctx, config, requests, func(taskID string, boundaryReached bool, commit HistoryCommit) error). The existing readBatchObject and validateBatchSnapshot work unchanged over a bufio.Reader on the pipe. This is viable because walkCommitChain already returns each task contiguously oldest-first (history.go:111-119) and cat-file --batch answers in request order, so the stream is already per-task ordered. In Validate, fold each commit straight into the current task Completion (the body of evaluate at validator.go:191-208), call cache.Record at the task boundary, and drop the completion. Subprocess count stays at 3 (tips batch, rev-list, cat-file batch), inside the MaxGitProcesses target of 12 (internal/perf/validation_scenarios.go:32). Close stdin at end of requests, drain stdout to EOF, and Wait on every path including validation failure; use exec.CommandContext so cancellation kills the child. Residual memory is the parent graph (roughly 8 MB at 50k commits) plus one decoded commit and one completion.
2. Index the DELETE: CREATE INDEX validated_commits_by_task ON validated_commits (validator_version, task_id). Keep the existing primary key as the duplicate-delivery guard; validated_commits is never SELECTed in normal operation, only INSERTed and DELETEd. Bump schemaVersion (cache.go:23); the cache is disposable and rebuildDatabase already handles regeneration (cache.go:579).
3. Fix the pre-size at operations.go:295 to an unsized map or one sized to an expected chain length.
4. Cheapen Record: prepare the INSERT once per transaction or use multi-row VALUES, and consider journal_mode WAL with synchronous NORMAL on this disposable cache. If WAL is enabled, mirror the -wal and -shm cleanup that the projection rebuild path currently omits (internal/projection/store.go:1140-1196 removes only the main temp file, while cache.go:589-593 removes all three).
5. Fallback if streaming gitstore is out of scope: chunk requests in Validate at 64 to 128 tasks per ReadTaskHistories call and release each chunk before the next. Memory becomes O(chunk x depth) but subprocess count becomes 3 per chunk, which breaks the MaxGitProcesses target. Streaming is the version that satisfies both axes.

Expected effect: peak resident memory bounded to the graph map plus O(1) commit state, independent of depth, and the task-axis slope returning toward 1.0.

## Acceptance

Re-running the scaling matrix and storage/resource measurements at the same fixture points shows a reduced task-count log-log slope and a bounded peak resident memory that does not grow proportionally with history depth, with deterministic SHA-1 and SHA-256 evidence and no change to validation results on any existing fixture.

Four measurement caveats found while checking that this is verifiable as written (2026-08-06):

- The two families do not share a fixture shape at the 500-by-100 point. The scaling matrix point is 525 total tasks (500 active plus 25 tombstoned); the storage run is 500 total with 475 active. The slope number and the resident-memory number therefore come from different fixtures. State this explicitly in the evidence, or pass --tasks 525 to the storage run and accept that it no longer compares to the 2026-07-30 baseline.
- Two depths give a ratio, not a bound. If "bounded" is to mean more than sub-proportional growth between two points, add depths, for example --storage-operations 20,50,100,200.
- Peak resident memory is not run-deterministic. "Deterministic evidence" here can only mean deterministic fixtures plus recorded provenance, not reproducible byte counts. Fixtures are deterministic (seeded ULIDs and fixed timestamps, internal/perf/fixture.go:25,149-174), so this is satisfiable, but say so rather than implying byte equality.
- The slope comparison against 1.102 and 1.555 is cross-run, and the environment block records no CPU model or host load. A large reduction is convincing; a marginal one is not strictly attributable. Within-run slopes normalize host speed, so prefer reporting those.

Two harness gaps worth closing in the same change, both small: the storage-resources full-validation invocation checks only the exit code and not the result content (internal/perf/storage.go:299-304), unlike the scaling path which asserts an exact literal oracle per sample (internal/perf/validation_scenarios.go:191-213); and the scaling phase never enforces the "commit must not be unknown" provenance gate that the acceptance phase applies (internal/cli main.go:347-349), so deterministic provenance for the scaling half currently depends on operator discipline.
